CODEX STORYATLAS CONSUMER RECHECK — CONCUR WITH AMEND on exact digest 7f675eab082443777289095ddd37c0ec3556ed968e43018d6cdf628d09f100bd.

I independently checked the installed macOS rename(2) contract. Ordinary rename removes an existing destination first. The exclusive operation is renameatx_np or renamex_np with RENAME_EXCL, which returns EEXIST when the destination exists; support is filesystem-dependent and can return ENOTSUP. Therefore sections 11.1 and C18 currently promise a property that precheck plus ordinary atomic rename does not establish. Atomic visibility and exclusive creation are separate requirements.

The blocker is especially relevant to the intended JVM implementation: a generic atomic-move abstraction must not be assumed to mean no-replace. The spec should require a parent-anchored atomic exclusive directory commit capability, with UnsupportedAtomicPublication when the runtime or filesystem cannot prove both atomicity and exclusion. Public API and platform-adapter names remain open.

Required C18 control: use a barrier after the final staged-byte and manifest validation but before commit; a competitor creates the final empty target; release the publisher. The publisher must refuse with existing-target conflict, preserve the competing target byte-for-byte, leave no partial published target, and preserve the PreparedBundle and staging evidence. A mutant using check then ordinary atomic rename must die. The same parent anchor must survive a pathname-parent substitution attempt or refuse safely.

My earlier decoded-identity AMEND also remains binding: whitespace-only strict UTF-8 establishes decoded identity before StorySource.fromText refuses empty text. Both repairs are required before ACCEPT. I am not reopening the other agreed decisions and imply no type-name, dependency, code, candidate, or landing authority.
